title: Investigate and remediate uneven quota enforcement causing customer 429 cascades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a capacity reshuffle on 2026-03-10 we observed uneven quota enforcement in the API gateway. Several tenants saw large spikes of 429 responses while other tenants were unaffected. The behavior looked like a cascading throttle: bursty clients were able to push through initial requests, then downstream quota checks rapidly rejected backlog requests, producing a short-lived 429 storm and elevated error rates for client SDKs that retried aggressively.

Why this ticket exists:
This is the follow-up to the on-call incident. We need a concrete root-cause analysis, short-term mitigations that are already in motion, and a prioritized set of action items to prevent recurrence. We also need to ensure rollout controls and tests exist before the next gateway deployment that touches quota logic.
timeline:
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - First error spike detected by SRE alerting (5xx and 429 increase)
2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - On-call engaged, traffic replays show burst queues building on gateway nodes
2026-03-10 02:21 UTC - Emergency config rollback of recent quota library change (release candidate deployed 2026-03-09)
2026-03-10 02:33 UTC - Temporary global whitelist for retries applied to reduce client-visible errors
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Traffic and error rates stabilized; monitoring left in enhanced sampling mode
root_cause: Primary cause: a race in the quota refresh path of the gateway introduced in commit 5b3f2a (quota:expire-ttl-refactor). When token-refresh requests and window-reset timers coincided, the local in-memory token buckets for some tenant shards were left transiently out-of-sync with the centralized lease store. A secondary factor: the new optimization bypassed tenant-level metrics in favor of aggregated counters, so the circuit that falls back to safe mode misclassified affected tenants and triggered a global fallback logic that over-throttled other tenants on overloaded nodes.
mitigation_summary:
Short-term: rolled back refactor, applied whitelist to reduce client-visible 429s, increased sampling for tenant quotas, and adjusted retry-backoff recommended settings in SDK docs.
Long-term: redesign quota refresh to be idempotent and add deterministic ordering for timer vs refresh; add tenant-scoped metrics back into fallback logic; add canary gating for quota library changes; add integration tests simulating concurrent token-refresh + window reset.
action_items: ENG-9121: Implement idempotent quota refresh (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-9122: Reintroduce tenant-level counters to fallback decision path (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-9123: Add chaos/integration test for token-refresh race (owner: Aaron Patel, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-9140: Add canary pipeline gating for gateway library changes (owner: SRE team lead - Nina Park, due: 2026-04-05)
DOC-ENG-56: Update SDK retry/backoff recommendations and note new transient-429 guidance (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-19)
observability_changes: Add tenant-scoped 95th/99th percentile token-bucket occupancy metrics to the gateway dashboard
Instrument refresh vs timer events with unique correlation IDs so we can trace races end-to-end
Create a dedicated 429-cascade alert that triggers on correlated tenant 429 spikes across >=3 nodes
